research_rationale: EO 6294 (September 18, 1933) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Transit Industry subject to two conditions. Condition (1) construes Article VII, paragraph 2 (existing labor contracts continue to their expiration dates, extensions may not exceed the code's maximum hours or fall below its minimum wages) and is a code-dependent qualification that the shared analysis would end on June 14, 1935. Condition (2), the direction to the American Transit Association to amend its By-laws, is a separate performance command whose end cannot be shown from held evidence, so the order is blocked rather than submitted with an unsupported end for that clause.
unresolved_material_gaps: ["Condition (2) directs the American Transit Association to amend its Constitution and By-laws 'as soon as possible after the effective date of this Code' so that, in the Administrator's judgment, there are no inequitable restrictions on membership. That is a one-time performance duty of a private association, not a continuing code term. The Transit Industry code's effective date is not held and no held source shows whether, when or to the Administrator's satisfaction the Association amended its By-laws, so its first end (exhaustion by performance, or the June 14, 1935 repeal if it was never performed) is not established. An order with a one-time contingent command beside the approval needs that command's own end or a block."]

The order recites that the Federal Alcohol Control Administration submitted certain amendments of the Brewing Industry code with its report, makes five findings, approves the amendments, and modifies the President's earlier approval of the code (the Executive Order of December 4, 1933) so that it covers the code in its entirety as amended. Original not yet held; the working text is a labeled transcription under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling.
